turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to give Owen a zero, and why did he find out on his phone in the middle of class?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, so that shows when it arrived, not who wrote it. And was Owen heard before you entered anything?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet, nowhere near his class. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Teenagers misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale; that's a bad citation, not proof of anything. And that's twice now you've walked past my question about whether he was heard.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll check that myself tonight. So what exactly are you proposing?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.

A forty-minute piece written cold against an essay done with the play open in front of him; of course one has quotations and the other doesn't. And I asked you a direct question, which you've now ignored. What are you proposing?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and Owen will do the rewrite to put this behind him, nothing more. Tonight's email says the zero comes off pending the rewrite, it happens privately with no other students present, nothing goes on his record either way, and it includes your apology for how he found out. Who else has seen this so far?
Will he do it?
I've said he will. Now answer my question: who else has seen this?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite with no other students present, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require your written apology for entering the zero before contacting me, and a full answer on who else has seen this and whether Owen was heard before the mark went in. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed that Owen would do a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight, the apology for how he found out, and to know who else has seen this; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting her to bring the other file, because that gave her something dated she could check rather than a claim.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, even after she asked three times, because an unanswered procedure question tells a litigator the process was skipped.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay just before midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after you owned entering the zero before calling her, say plainly whether and when you spoke to Owen, so her procedure question is settled before you show the version history.
